title: A frequency-dependent boundary trace estimate
source_hypothesis: Local H1 field with actual Pu in L2; smooth scalar-principal second-order CAA glancing system, noncharacteristic boundary, arbitrary complex lower matrices, fixed nested compact physical and conic patches. No boundary condition is required.
reviewed_arguments: The global smooth auxiliary frequencies define the normal scale kappa and the boundary-layer weight L. All four scale inequalities and both Sobolev inclusions are proved directly.
Two exact moments cancel the unknown normal derivative. The Taylor remainder, its sign and the constants 8 and 2/105 are proved before selecting a frequency-dependent interval.
The sharp output-frequency indicator is used only as a measurable multiplier. It is never differentiated or treated as an ordinary symbol.
Full Fourier-kernel estimates retain all input frequencies. Lipschitz control of m bounds the noncommuting boundary factor; q kappa <= tau controls the arbitrary normal order-two remainder.
Arbitrary complex lower matrices and the actual L2 residual are retained. No natural-dual source is silently upgraded to L2.

The weak-domain proof uses bounded Fourier balls, the distributional equation, scalar Fubini and monotone convergence. It identifies the result with the actual continuous L2 value trace without presupposing smooth solution approximation.

A real collar flow removes the principal normal cross block, moves all tangential variables, and fixes the boundary. Complete covector substitution, Jacobians and first-order coordinate terms are retained.
The actual boundary eikonal identities give the exact transported principal factor minus mu lambda times a positive degree-zero coefficient.

A fixed q-independent inverse graph intertwines the tangential principal operator up to an order-one FIO with full smooth remainders. Matching principal symbols on the whole supported larger graph prevents an omitted order-two cutoff error.
All equation errors after coordinates and graph composition are bounded in L2 by the local energy and actual source. Nested physical cutoffs cover the source, operator inputs and commutator supports.
The theorem applies to the actual boundary value of every local H1 field with Pu in L2 in the stated CAA glancing class. It requires no boundary condition or lower-matrix commutativity.
Explicit moderation with exponent 11/6 proves ordinary localization in the layer space. Physical cutoffs use actual graph composition and retained coarse smooth errors.

The exact stable-norm identity separates the proved layer term from the still unresolved oscillating term for general solutions. Neither complete stable-weight recovery nor general PDE representation is claimed.

Three solutions prove the trace constants, the necessity of equation control and a full differential coordinate example including its imaginary lower-order term. Twenty-five exact symbolic checks accompany the analytic proofs.

All fourteen final lesson captures were inspected, including eleven overlapping desktop views, the whole figure and two mobile samples. All 278 formulas and 24 displays parse and horizontal extents remain accessible.
The 102 required human foundation proofs remain external. Full weighted recovery, controlled residual removal, general energy representation and every other full AN-04 obligation remain active.
